# How to Get a Library Card

A library card is free for anyone who lives, works, or goes to school in the
Maplewood area. It unlocks borrowing, the public computers, and the whole
[[using-the-elibrary-app|digital collection]].

## What You Need

Bring one item that shows your **name** and one that shows your **current
address** — a photo ID plus a piece of mail is the usual combination. If your ID
already shows your current address, that single item is enough. Children can get
a card with a parent or guardian present to sign.

## Where to Sign Up

You can register in person at the circulation desk of any branch. Hours differ
by location, so check before you go — ask the assistant for `get_hours`, and use
`get_contact` for the circulation desk phone number if you want to call ahead.

If you would rather start online, you can pre-register on the library website and
finish at any desk; you only need to show your documents once.

## After You Have a Card

- Your first card is free. There is a small charge to replace a lost card — the
  assistant can quote the current amount with `get_fee`.
- Set a PIN at the desk. You will need your card number and PIN to log in to the
  catalog and to [[using-the-elibrary-app|the eLibrary app]].
- You are responsible for items checked out on your card, so report a lost card
  promptly. See [[fines-and-fees]] for how lost and overdue items are handled.

> [!tip] No proof of address?
> Students, people experiencing homelessness, and new arrivals can still get a
> card — talk to the circulation desk about alternative verification. Reach them
> through `get_contact`.

result.content:
# Borrowing, Holds, and Renewals

Once you have a [[getting-a-library-card|library card]], borrowing is
self-service. The exact loan length and how many times you can renew depend on
the item type and are always shown on the item's page in the catalog and in
**My Account** — check there rather than guessing.

## Checking Out

Bring your items and your card to a self-checkout station or the circulation
desk. Most physical items check out on the spot. For digital items, see
[[using-the-elibrary-app|the eLibrary app]].

## Placing a Hold

If an item is out or lives at another branch, place a **hold** and the library
will route it to your pickup branch:

1. Find the item in the online catalog.
2. Choose **Place Hold** and pick your pickup branch.
3. You will be notified when it arrives, and it will wait for you on the holds
   shelf for several days before being released to the next person.

Holds are the easiest way to gather materials from across all three branches in
one place. **My Account** lists your holds and shows when one is ready to pick
up, and staff at any branch's circulation desk can help.

## Renewing

Items renew automatically unless someone else is waiting or you have hit the
renewal limit. You can also renew manually from **My Account**. If an item will
not renew, it is usually because there is a hold behind it.

> [!note] We are fine-free
> Maplewood does not charge daily overdue fines. You will not rack up a balance
> for a late book. You are still responsible for returning items and for the
> cost of anything lost or damaged — the details, and any current charges, are
> in [[fines-and-fees]] (amounts come from `get_fee`).

# Borrowing eBooks and Audiobooks

Your [[getting-a-library-card|library card]] comes with a full digital library
you can use from your phone or tablet through the **eLibrary app**, free for every
cardholder — no trip to a branch required.

## Get Set Up

1. Install the eLibrary app from your device's app store.
2. Choose **Maplewood Public Library** when it asks for your library.
3. Sign in with your **card number and PIN** (the same ones you set up at the
   desk).

## Borrowing

- Search or browse, then tap **Borrow**. The title downloads to your device.
- Titles return themselves at the end of the loan, so there is nothing late and
  nothing to bring back — which pairs nicely with our [[fines-and-fees|fine-free
  policy]] anyway.
- If a popular title is checked out, place a **hold** just like with
  [[borrowing-holds-and-renewals|physical items]] and you will be notified when
  it is ready.

## Reading and Listening

The app reads ebooks and plays audiobooks in one place, remembers where you left
off across devices, and works offline once a title is downloaded. Everything you
finish here counts toward the [[summer-reading-program|Summer Reading Program]].

> [!tip] Trouble signing in?
> The most common snag is a forgotten PIN. Reset it at any branch or by calling
> the circulation desk — find the number with `get_contact`.

Book a session of [[summer-reading-program|one-on-one tech help]] for hands-on
guidance, or reach the reference desk through `get_contact`.

# Fines and Fees

**Maplewood Public Library is fine-free.** We do not charge daily overdue fines
on items you return late. This has been our policy since the board eliminated
overdue fines, and it replaces any older fee schedule you may have seen on a
flyer or an out-of-date page.

Going fine-free does not mean there are no responsibilities — it means a late
return will not quietly grow into a balance that keeps you from using the
library.

## What We Do *Not* Charge

- **Daily overdue fines.** Returning an item after its due date does not cost
  money. (If you want to confirm, the assistant can read the current overdue
  rate with `get_fee` — it is zero.)

## What You *Are* Responsible For

- **Lost or damaged items.** If an item is not returned or comes back damaged,
  you are charged a replacement cost so the next person can still borrow it.
- **A replacement card** if you lose yours (your first card is free).
- **Printing and copies**, and **meeting-room reservations** for non-community
  bookings — see [[printing-and-computers]].

For any of these, the assistant quotes the **current amount with `get_fee`**
rather than repeating a number here, because prices change and a stale number on
this page would be worse than none.

> [!important] Returning the item clears it
> Because we are fine-free, simply returning a late item settles it. A
> replacement charge for a *lost* item is removed if you later find and return it
> in good condition.

results.response:
No, that's out of date. Maplewood Public Library is **fine-free**, so you won't be charged anything for returning a book late. The current overdue fine is **$0.00 per day** ([borrowing policy](https://example.org/policies/borrowing)).

The 25-cent daily fine was replaced when the library board got rid of overdue fines. A late return no longer adds up to a balance that stops you from using the library. Once you bring the item back, you're all set.

You can still be charged in a few cases:
- **Lost or damaged items:** you pay a replacement cost. If you later find a lost item and return it in good condition, that charge is removed.
- **A replacement card** if you lose yours. Your first card is free.
- **Printing, copies and some meeting-room bookings.**

*Source: "Fines and Fees (We Are Fine-Free)" wiki page and the library's borrowing policy.*

If you'd like to know the current price for any of those, just ask and I'll look it up.
